spotlights.title: Popcorn 2026 Scouts!
spotlights.body:
Did you know that popcorn sales are the greatest contributor to the overall financial sustainability of Troop 8? By selling popcorn, you allow Troop 8 to have the best equipment and go on the most amazing camping trips each year! Popcorn sales are also a great way to build up your personal Scout account, which you can use to pay for campouts and high adventure trips.

Troop 8 is participating in the Trails End popcorn fundraiser again this year. Returning scouts should log in to their Trails End account on the web (portal.trails-end.com) or via the mobile app. Scouts new to selling popcorn with Troop 8 need to register (or update their registration) with Trails End — be sure your unit code is updated to ZCUXT so you are part of the Troop 8 program.

Send your personal Trails End sales webpage to family and friends to help support you — online sales can start immediately. On the app or website, register for an upcoming Troop 8 storefront sales opportunity starting as early as September 5; multiple storefront shifts are available between now and the end of October.

This year's Troop 8 goal is to sell $35,000 worth of popcorn. Every Scout is asked to sell at least $150 worth of popcorn — sales above $150 count toward your Scout account, and there are prizes to earn (Amazon gift cards, etc.) along the way. Remember, you aren't selling popcorn, you're selling Scouting. Get out there and sell!

Any questions, contact Mr. Wade (lankfordw@gmail.com — be sure to copy a parent). Unit Code: ZCUXT

YIS,
Mr. Wade

spotlights.title: Venture Patrol: Fall Backyard Adventures
spotlights.body:
Chicken Bird Dog Squirrel Venture Patrollers! While everyone is focused on their last week of summer break, the Venture Patrol is already turning its focus to firing up the engine on our fall Backyard Adventures series — two epic trips on the horizon.

Expedition Alpha: Leaf Peeping in the St. Regis Canoe Wilderness (Adirondacks, NY). Classic North Country canoeing, multi-pond portaging, and backcountry skills under a canopy of fall foliage. Dates: roll out early Saturday, September 19th, back Monday, September 21st (no school!). Cost: approx. $400 per Venture Patroller. Crew size: 5 scouts & 3 adults (limited by NYSDEC). Note: this trip overlaps directly with Troop 8's Sea Girt campout, so you'll need to choose one.

Expedition Bravo: Whitewater Kayaking at Zoar on the Deerfield River (Charlemont, MA). Navigating Class I-II features (maybe some III's), catching eddies, and progressing skills toward the "Gap." Dates: leave Friday afternoon, October 9th, back late Sunday night, October 11th (no school on 10/12!). Cost: approx. $615 per Venture Patroller. Crew size: 9 scouts & 3 adults.

Because crew sizes are strictly limited by the NYSDEC and the Zoar outfitters, if you want to claim a spot on either trip (or both), fill out the Google form to express interest or submit a deposit to make a firm commitment. See you on the water.

Mr. Erb, Cell: 440.725.0649

spotlights.title: Sea Girt Campout — 5th Beach Kickoff
spotlights.body:
Saturday, September 19 – Sunday, September 20, 2026.

Departure: Saturday morning, September 19th from Ogden, 7:08am. Return: Sunday, September 20th, time TBD (estimate noon). Gear Pull: Wednesday, September 16th at 7:08pm at Ogden.

Cost: $35 per person. Meals: Scouts should eat before arrival at Ogden on 9/19 or bring a bagged breakfast; Patrols provide Saturday lunch & dinner and Sunday breakfast.

Clothing/Special Gear: Proper clothing and beach footwear are a must — bathing suit, sun swim shirt, sunscreen, beach gear, towel, and bug repellent. Dress for cool beach winds; volleyball games likely, and fishing is available with personal surf fishing gear. See the Sea Girt Flyer for more details.

Dr. Turbin, ASM — (973) 476-0604, rturbin@verizon.net

spotlights.title: Service Projects
spotlights.body:
“Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.” — Helen Keller

The 2026 SERV Award year runs from January 1st to December 31, 2026. Check the newsletter often, as it is never too early to start earning service hours for 2026! Scouts will announce ongoing service projects at the meetings. Please support your fellow scouts and the community by volunteering your time!

Please visit the Service Project page on the Troop 8 website for more information and the updated policy regarding Service Project requirements for Star and Life.

spotlights.title: 2027 Florida Sea Base Out Island Adventure
spotlights.body:
April 10 – April 16, 2027. Contact Mr. Haller at 215.704.7974 (drewhaller@yahoo.com) or Mr. Kamionek at 201.207.5821 (skamionek@gmail.com).

Live on an island in the Keys for a week like Robinson Crusoe — paddle in 12-foot war canoes to Big Munson Island with all personal gear stowed in a dry bag (5.5 miles over open ocean water, so pack light and come ready to paddle). Days ashore include fishing, snorkeling, and kayaking, sleeping in tents or hammocks, with a seafood luau and patch presentation to close out the trip.

Scouts must be First Class and 13 years old by April 10, 2027. This Interest Form must be turned in with a $200 deposit by September 1, 2026 and will be reviewed for eligibility by the Scoutmaster. Estimated cost is approximately $2,600 — Scout (popcorn) accounts can be used to help pay for this trip.

spotlights.title: New Cell Phone Policy
spotlights.body: Troop 8 leadership recently evaluated how cell phone use is impacting the scouting experience for the boys and everyone involved. Based on this assessment, the Committee approved a new Cell Phone Policy, available for download.
